newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1997 palm oil demand seen around 480,000 t.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1997 palm oil demand seen around 480,000 t.

text.p: Thailand's demand for crude palm oil in 1997 is expected to remain at this year's level of 480,000 tonnes or move slightly higher, an official said on Wednesday.
Somsak Kositset, secretary-general of Thai Palm Oil Refinery Association, told Reuters the industry might import less next year due to the current high stock of about 60,000-70,000 tonnes.
The liberalisation of soybean imports, effective since November 1, is likely to put pressure on palm oil demand that normally grows by 10-15 percent annually, he said.

"We will have to look at the stock again by the end of December to see if imports are necessasry," Somsak said. "If we can procure around 30,000 tonnes of crude from domestic sources during the low season, and if the demand continues at this rate, there would be no need to import."
Thailand normally imports crude palm oil in December and February, the low season of palm harvesting. It imported about 25,000 tonnes of crude palm oil this year, according to Somsak.
